author.name: Leo Tolstoy
author.biography: An aristocrat who became a soldier, landowner and celebrated novelist, Tolstoy acquired many of the advantages other people dream of. He also became a searching critic of status, violence and the ways a successful life can fail to answer its deepest questions. Tolstoy's own crisis over death and the meaning of success sharpened this novella. A respectable official becomes the measure of a world that knows how to advance and little about how to die.

hook.text: What if you discover too late that you have lived the wrong life?

paragraphs: Ivan Ilyich has done what was expected. He has built a career, married suitably and learned how to make his home look right. Then illness makes those achievements strangely powerless.

Tolstoy begins with other people's response to Ivan's death, so the suspense lies elsewhere: in what it feels like to be the person dying. Polite reassurance can become a form of abandonment. A conversation about symptoms can avoid the question everyone knows is there. People who share a room may inhabit completely different realities.

The novella makes ordinary habits newly visible. Which pleasures mattered? Which choices were made because they were considered proper? What kind of company can someone offer when they cannot repair what is happening?

Its brevity gives these questions an unusual force. There is little room to hide in an elaborate life story. Read it while the questions are still available to you as choices: what would have to change if a successful life were no longer a sufficient answer?

orientation.text: The opening announces Ivan's death. The story then returns to his life and illness; knowing the outcome is essential to its design.
